subject: Developer-gated deploy primer and artifact list for assessor
messages:
From: Bethany Greene <bethany@assessors.io>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: FiscusBank SOC2 Team <soc2@soc2.fiscusbank.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request – developer-gated deploys and approvals

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier. For the SOC2 assessment we need a concise package showing how Redwood enforces developer-gated deploys for production artifacts. Specifically the assessor is asking for:
- PR approval policy (who can approve, automatic checks)
- CI/CD gate evidence (approval logs from the last 30 days)
- Secrets scanning and ephemeral credential usage in pipelines
- Change authorization matrix and emergency rollback policy

Could you send the artefacts and any short explainer (1–2 pages) that ties them together? If a Drive folder or short runbook exists, a link is fine. We prefer minimal PDFs or CSVs rather than big bundles.

Best,
Bethany
Bethany Greene
Senior Assessor, Lighthouse Assessors

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Bethany Greene <bethany@assessors.io>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request – developer-gated deploys and approvals

Bethany —

Thanks, attaching a short primer and point-by-point artefacts. Quick summary so you can route to the right reviewers:

1) PR & approval policy: we require at least one codeowner approval for prod branches; PR must pass automated checks (lint, unit tests, secrets-scan) before it becomes mergeable. Exceptions are handled via change-authority tickets (see runbook link).

2) CI/CD gate evidence: I’ve exported our approval logs for the last 30 days (ci-approval-log-20260825.csv). The CSV includes PR number, approver, approver role (dev, eng-lead, security), pipeline run id, and timestamp.

3) Secrets management: we use ephemeral short-lived tokens injected via the runner credentials service and enforce secret scanning at build time. Included is a recent secrets-scan snapshot that shows the scans and remediation flags.

4) Change matrix & rollback: attached primer outlines authorization tiers (developer, team lead, change board) and the emergency rollback workflow.

Attachments: developer-gated-deploy-primer.pdf; ci-approval-log-20260825.csv; secrets-scan-snapshot-20260828.json

If you want, Jordan can pull a small sample of PRs and link to traceable commits/merge timestamps.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Bethany Greene <bethany@assessors.io>, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request – developer-gated deploys and approvals

Hi Bethany —

Following up with a brief machine-readable excerpt and clarifying notes you requested. A few clarifications up-front to avoid confusion:
- "Approval" in our pipeline is explicit: a user with merge rights clicks an Approve button in our CI UI; approval is stored in the pipeline audit and can’t be bypassed.
- Automated checks are enforced as required checks on the branch. If any required check fails, the PR cannot be merged.

I exported a CSV with the last 30 days of approvals, and added a column (approval_type) where we indicate if the approval was manual or via an automated canary promotion. Sample rows attached.

Also note the special-case "emergency patch" procedure:
- Emergency patches require a high-urgency ticket and post-facto review within 24 hours by the change board.
- Emergency approvals are recorded with an escalation flag in the audit log (see ci-approval-log).

If the assessor wants individual PR HTML threads or commit SHAs for traceability, tell me which PR numbers and I’ll extract them.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Platform Engineer, CI/CD

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Bethany Greene <bethany@assessors.io>, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request – developer-gated deploys and approvals

Bethany —

Adding short answers to a couple of likely assessor questions:

Q: How do you ensure secrets are not leaked into build logs?
A: Runner-side masking removes secrets from console output; we also redact artifact metadata before storage and prevent artifact uploads that contain unmasked secret patterns. The secrets-scan snapshot shows the latest scan results and remediation tickets.

Q: How do you validate that production deploys used tagged artifacts?
A: Our deploy pipeline requires an artifact signature step: artifacts are signed in the build step and deploys refuse unsigned artifacts. We keep signature attestations in the artifact registry.

If you want the artifact-signature extracts, I can add a short CSV sample.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Platform Security

From: Bethany Greene <bethany@assessors.io>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request – developer-gated deploys and approvals

Team —

This is great, thank you. I reviewed the primer and the CSV sample. Two quick follow-ups before I close the control:
1) Can you provide one signed artifact attestation (CSV extract) from a production deploy in the last 90 days?
2) Can you redact and share the post-facto emergency patch review notes for a single emergency that occurred in the last 6 months (redact PII and internal IPs)?

If you can drop both items in the Drive link you sent by EOD Wednesday PT, I’ll be able to finalize the evidence packet for the assessor team.

Regards,
Bethany
